newsitem.title: USA: OMAP Holdings sets 1-for-30 reverse split.
newsitem.headline: OMAP Holdings sets 1-for-30 reverse split.

text.p: OMAP Holdings Inc said Tuesday it would effect a one-for-30 reverse stock split and change its name to China Food and Beverage Co.
It said its stock symbol has been changed to CHIF, in the over-the-counter bulletin board, to reflect its new name.

On March 17 the company said it had acquired China Development Corp, a private investment firm based in the Bahamas. China Development owns a 60 percent stake in Nantong Aitesi Beer Co Ltd, based in Qidong City in China's Jiangsu Province.
Giving effect to the acquisition and the reverse split, OMAP said its total outstanding common shares now stands at 2,514,900, of which 216,955 are publicly floated.

The company operates a subsdiary, Establissements R. Kohl, based in Calais, France, that manufacturers and distributes vending machines, electrical heaters, electrical light fixtures and paper processing equipment.
